title: Module template + style/accessibility guide (WCAG 2.2 AA, i18n-ready)
context: Every curriculum module must follow a consistent, quality-structural template so modules are cheap and uniform to author. The template instantiates the seven required sections, a style guide, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility requirements, and i18n-readiness conventions so that quality is structural rather than per-author. Baking accessibility and i18n into the template from M0 prevents expensive retrofit later. The template depends on the framework (framework-001) and is a blocking prerequisite for all module authoring tasks.
objective: Create the canonical module template with all seven required sections and a companion style/accessibility guide covering WCAG 2.2 AA compliance and i18n-readiness conventions, ready to serve as the basis for all subsequent modules.
acceptanceCriteria: Template includes all seven required sections: (1) learning objectives, (2) lesson narrative, (3) hands-on exercise, (4) worked example, (5) checklist/takeaway artifact, (6) formative assessment, and (7) instructor notes.
Each section has placeholder text, instructions, and an example showing the expected content and length.

Style guide covers heading structure, alt-text requirements, colorblind-safe figure guidance (specific palette recommendation), plain-language conventions for non-computational scientists, and inline citation format.
WCAG 2.2 AA requirements enumerated for each section type (text, code blocks, figures, exercises).
i18n-readiness guidelines documented: no hard-coded locale-specific strings in examples; text extractable for translation; date/unit/number formats locale-neutral.
Template is committed to the project repo and references framework-001; DCO signed off; reviewed and signed off by Educator reviewer.
resources: Bloom's taxonomy (revised); Understanding by Design (Wiggins & McTighe)
output: A canonical MODULE-TEMPLATE.md and STYLE-GUIDE.md committed to the project repo, defining the seven required sections with placeholder content and the style, accessibility, and i18n conventions all module authors must follow.
